column1: # clues.tsv for ft_strlen — hints only, never answers.
# Format: <hint><TAB><member CASE label><TAB>...   (fires if ANY member case fails)
Where does a C string end? You have to walk it one byte at a time until you reach that marker. Two questions: what marks the end, and does that marker itself count toward the length?

Spaces, tabs, digits and bytes above 0x7f (UTF-8 text is made of them) are ordinary bytes — they are part of the string. If a length looks too small, are you stopping early on a byte you think is "not a real character", or on one whose value a plain char holds as negative?
No string has a limit on its length. Is there one your function cannot count? For every variable it uses, and any room it sets aside: what is the largest length that one can hold?
